chunks: He said: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh, may Allah have mercy on him, reported to me from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from Bashir al-Kunasi, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon them both, said to me:

O Abu Khalid, there will surely come trials and tribulations like pieces of the dark night, from which no one will be saved except the one whose covenant Allah has taken. Those are the lamps of guidance and the springs of knowledge; Allah will save them from every dark trial.

It is as though I see your master, having risen above the hill of your Najaf, destined for Kufa, with three hundred and some odd over ten men, Jibrail on his right, Mikail on his left, and Israfil ahead of him, carrying with him the standard of the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, unfurled. He does not aim it at any people except that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, destroys them.

key_terms.راية رسول الله: Rayat Rasul Allah (the Prophet's standard) — the banner of the Prophet Muhammad, carried by the Mahdi
key_terms.فتن: Fitan (trials/tribulations) — periods of severe social and spiritual upheaval
key_terms.مصابيح الهدى: Masabih al-Huda (lamps of guidance) — metaphor for righteous leaders who illuminate the path
key_terms.ميثاق: Mithaq (covenant) — God's covenant taken from believers, binding them to truth
key_terms.ينابيع العلم: Yanabi al-Ilm (springs of knowledge) — metaphor for sources of divine knowledge

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Zayn al-Abidin say about the Mahdi and the trials before his rising?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) prophesied to his companion Abu Khalid al-Kabuli about a future time of overwhelming tribulations, from which only those who hold fast to God's covenant will be saved. He then described the rising of the Mahdi (AS) at Najaf near Kufa, accompanied by 313 men and the archangels Jibrail, Mikail, and Israfil, carrying the Prophet's banner, with which no people can withstand. This hadith, narrated through a chain of prominent Shia scholars, is one of the key traditions about the advent of the Mahdi in Shia eschatology.
word_analysis: may Allah have mercy on him

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 5. He said: Abul Qasim Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Qawlawayh, may Allah bless him with mercy, reported to me from his father, from Sa’d ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Maskan, from Bashir al-Kannasi, from Abu Khalid al-Kabuli who said: ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn, peace be upon him, told me:

"O Abu Khalid, there will come a time of trials and tribulations, (descending) like a piece of dark night, from which no one will be safe, except the one holding the covenant of Allah. These people will be the guiding lights and the sources of knowledge, whom Allah will have saved from all the dark temptations.

As if I see your master, rising above the hill of your Najaf destined for Kufa, with three hundred and some odd over ten men, Jibraeel on his right, Mikaeel on his left, Israfil ahead of him, and with him (is) the Prophet’s standard, unfurled, to whichever people he aims with it, they are destroyed by Allah."
